name: mac-wf2
prompt:
kk-engine (C++20, Vulkan through volk, CMake + Ninja) gets a macOS CI job that builds natively on a 2018 Intel MacBook Air (macOS 14, Apple clang 16 from the Command Line Tools, MoltenVK from the runner's $VULKAN_SDK, a Forgejo runner with label macos-amd64 in host mode, started on demand). Speed does not matter there, quality does. Write the new Forgejo workflow .forgejo/workflows/macos.yml (Forgejo Actions, GitHub Actions syntax), replacing the file's old content. Take the step style of .forgejo/workflows/release.yml (given: its linux job's Configure, Build, No warnings anywhere and Unit tests steps).
1. Header comment: macOS (Intel) build and tests natively on the Mac runner (label macos-amd64: a 2018 MacBook Air, macOS 14, Apple clang, MoltenVK); it builds the engine, every demo and the unit tests there, runs the tests on MoltenVK and keeps the x86_64 package as an artifact; the Mac's runner is started on demand, so this runs only by hand (no schedule), and a dispatch waits in the queue while the Mac is off; the Mac is slow (2 cores), which is fine.
2. `name: macOS`; `on:` only `workflow_dispatch:`; `concurrency:` group `macos`, cancel-in-progress false; `env:` KKE_JOBS "4" (2 cores, 4 threads, 8 GB RAM) and VERSION macos-test.
3. One job `build`: runs-on macos-amd64, timeout-minutes 480, no container. Steps:
   a. actions/checkout@v4.
   b. `Tools`: run `cmake --version`, `ninja --version`, `glslangValidator --version`, `clang --version` (so a missing tool fails here, by name).
   c. `Configure`: `set -o pipefail`, then cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DKKE_ENABLE_FEMFX=ON -DKKE_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON -DKKE_ENABLE_VALIDATION=OFF "-DKKE_VERSION_NAME=$VERSION" 2>&1 | tee configure.log (continue lines with ` \` as release.yml does).
   d. `Build`: set -o pipefail; cmake --build build -j "$KKE_JOBS" 2>&1 | tee build.log.
   e. `No warnings anywhere`: tools/ci/check_warnings.sh configure.log build.log.
   f. `Unit tests`: a comment (volk opens libvulkan.dylib at run time; macOS drops DYLD_* variables when it starts a system program such as /bin/bash, so it is set inside the step), then run: `export DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH="${VULKAN_SDK:+$VULKAN_SDK/lib:}/usr/local/lib:/usr/lib"`, `mkdir -p results`, `./build/bin/kke_tests --gtest_brief=1 --gtest_output=json:results/kke_tests.json 2>&1 | tee results/kke_tests.log` with set -o pipefail first.
   g. `Package`: `tools/packaging/package.sh --bin build/bin --platform macos --version "$VERSION" --out dist --deps build/_deps` (no --strip).
   h. `https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/upload-artifact@v4` with name macos-package, path dist/.
   i. `https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/upload-artifact@v4` with `if: always()`, name macos-tests, path results/.
Nothing else: no other jobs, no cross-compiling, no Docker image.
